title: Contributing
search: # Contributing Thanks for helping out. The project is a single package, so the loop is short: edit, test, build, document. ## Repository layout ```text vue-contribution-graph-3d/ ├── src/ │ ├── components/ Vue components (one file per component) │ ├── composables/ useGitHubContributions, useContributionStats, … │ ├── three/ ContributionScene + the growth animator │ ├── utils/ Pure logic: normalize, levels, stats, sample, format │ ├── constants.ts Sizes, durations, level thresholds │ ├── themes.ts Palettes, scene colors, theme resolution │ ├── tokens.css Tailwind @theme tokens + attribute overrides │ ├── style.css The stylesheet shipped as dist/style.css │ └── index.ts Public entry point ├── tests/ Vitest suites, one file per module ├── docs/ Vue + Vite site and playground ├── vite.config.ts Library build (ES + CJS + .d.ts) └── vitest.config.ts jsdom environment ``` ## Getting started ```sh npm install npm run dev # Vue + Vite dev server → http://localhost:5173 npm run test:watch # Vitest in watch mode ``` ## Scripts | Script | What it does | | ---------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | `npm run dev` | Documentation site with hot reload. | | `npm run build` | Build `dist/` (ES, CJS, `.d.ts`, `style.css`). | | `npm run typecheck` | `vue-tsc --noEmit` over source, tests and theme. | | `npm test` | Run the Vitest suite once. | | `npm run test:watch` | Vitest in watch mode. | | `npm run docs:build` | Static build of the documentation. | | `npm run format` | Prettier, over everything. | | `npm run format:check` | CI-friendly formatting check. | Run `npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build && npm run docs:build` before opening a pull request — that is exactly what `prepublishOnly` runs. ## Coding style - **TypeScript, strict.** No `any` in public signatures; internal escapes need a comment. - **Prettier, no ESLint.** Formatting is `printWidth: 100`, single quotes, no semicolons, trailing commas. Let the editor run Prettier on save. - **Vue single-file components** with ` ` and the `defineOptions` name. - **Doc comments on every public export.** They are what the API pages and the generated `.d.ts` show. ## Testing Logic lives in `src/utils` and `src/three/growth.ts` precisely so it can be tested without WebGL. When you add a feature: 1. Keep the pure part pure — no `THREE.*` in `utils/`. 2. Add a test next to the matching file in `tests/`. 3. Inject `fetchFn` in network tests; never let a unit test hit the network. ```ts import { computeStats } from '../src/utils/stats' expect(computeStats(days)).toEqual({ total: 12, activeDays: 4, … }) ``` Component tests use `@vue/test-utils` and assert on attributes, emitted events and accessible markup rather than CSS. ## Documentation Every feature needs a page in `docs/`. Add the prop to the component page, add the option to the composables table, and add a runnable example when the feature is interactive. The docs import the library through an alias to `src/`, so an example that runs in `npm run dev` runs for consumers too. ## Three.js etiquette - **Dispose everything you create.** Geometries, materials, canvas textures, controls, observers, listeners and the `requestAnimationFrame` handle all have to go in `dispose()`. - **Never dispose shared objects.** `THREE.Sprite` shares one module-level geometry — disposing it would break every other sprite in the page. - **Keep the animation loop allocation free.** The per-frame work must not create objects; adapter arrays are rebuilt only when the data changes. ## Pull request checklist - [ ] `npm run typecheck` passes. - [ ] `npm test` passes, with tests for new behaviour. - [ ] `npm run build` and `npm run docs:build` succeed. - [ ] `npm run format` was run. - [ ] New props, events and slots are documented. - [ ] `dispose()` still releases anything the change created. ## Reporting bugs Open an issue with the component, the props you passed, the browser and a way to reproduce it. A reproducible sandbox or a failing test is worth a dozen screenshots.

title: Working with data
search: # Working with data ## The day grid Every component consumes the same flat array of days: ```ts interface ContributionDay { date: string // "2025-09-21" count: number // contributions that day week: number // column index, 0 = first week of the year weekday: number // row index, 0 = Sunday isFuture: boolean // has not happened yet isOutsideYear: boolean // padding from a neighbouring year } ``` Days are laid out Sunday-first in a rectangular grid. Padding days from December of the previous year and January of the next one are kept so the grid stays `weeks × 7` — they always carry `count: 0`. You rarely build this by hand: ```ts import { normalizeContributionData } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const days = normalizeContributionData( [ { date: '2025-09-21', count: 4 }, { date: '2025-09-22', count: 9 }, ], 2025, ) ``` ## From the GitHub API `useGitHubContributions` wraps the community [github-contributions-api](https://github-contributions-api.jogruber.de/) endpoint, which needs no token and returns the whole history in one request. ```ts import { useGitHubContributions } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const { username, // Ref year, // Ref years, // Ref newest first days, // Ref status, // Ref error, // Ref loading, // Ref load, // (handle?: string) => Promise setYear, // (year: string | number) => void reload, // () => void } = useGitHubContributions({ username: () => 'torvalds' }) ``` ### Options | Option | Type | Default | Description | | ---------- | ------------------ | ------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | `username` | `MaybeRefOrGetter` | `''` | Reactive handle; `@` is stripped automatically. | | `year` | `MaybeRefOrGetter` | current | Reactive year to display. | | `autoLoad` | `boolean` | `true` | Fetch on creation and whenever the handle changes. | | `fetchFn` | `typeof fetch` | global | Inject your own `fetch` (tests, proxies, mocks). | If the requested year does not exist for that user, the newest available year is selected automatically. Stale responses are discarded, so typing quickly through a search box can never overwrite a newer result with an older one. ### Using it inside ` ` ```vue (error = message)" /> ``` The component creates the composable for you. Use the template-ref API when you also need the years in a ` `. ## Aggregating statistics ```ts import { useContributionStats, computeStats } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const stats = useContributionStats(() => days.value) // { total, activeDays, longestStreak, bestDay } ``` `computeStats` is the pure version if you do not want a `ComputedRef`. Future days and padding days are excluded, so a year in progress is never skewed by months that have not happened yet. ## Sample data `useSampleContributions` produces a deterministic year — the same seed always yields the same grid, so demos and screenshots stay stable. ```ts import { useSampleContributions } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const days = useSampleContributions(2025) // every day is in the past → full grid const custom = useSampleContributions(2026, 42) // different seed ``` Because it is deterministic you can unit test against it, and it makes offline development possible. ## Your own source Anything that produces `{ date, count }` pairs works: ```ts import { normalizeContributionData, computeStats } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const payload = await fetch('/api/activity').then((r) => r.json()) const days = normalizeContributionData(payload.entries, 2025) const stats = computeStats(days) ``` Then hand `days` to ` ` and `stats` to ` `. ## Height scale Bars are scaled logarithmically so that quiet days stay visible: ```ts height = 0.24 + (log1p(count) / log1p(maxCount)) * (10.5 - 0.24) ``` - `count === 0` renders a `0.1` tall placeholder instead of disappearing. - The busiest day always reaches the full `10.5` units. - The color level is bucketed independently: `0`, `1–3`, `4–7`, `8–13`, `14+`. Both functions are exported (`getBarHeight`, `getContributionLevel`) if you need to render the same values elsewhere — for example in a 2D fallback.

Already own the data? Pass an array of days through `data` instead — read [Working with data](./data) for the exact format. ## Load a real profile Bind the handle to a `ref` when it comes from your own form: ```vue ``` The component owns the request, the loading spinner, the error state and the active year, and exposes them through a template ref: ```vue ``` | Exposed | Type | Description | | ---------------- | ---------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `years` | `Ref ` | Available years, newest first. | | `year` | `Ref ` | The year currently rendered. | | `setYear(year)` | `(year: string \| number) => void` | Switch the grid to another year. | | `load(username)` | `Promise ` | Fetch another profile. | | `reload()` | `() => void` | Re-fetch the current profile. | | `status` | `Ref ` | `idle`, `loading`, `success` or `error`. | | `error` | `Ref ` | Human readable failure message. | | `replay()` | `() => void` | Restart the grow animation. | | `resetView()` | `() => void` | Move the camera back to the default framing. | | `ready` | `Ref ` | The WebGL scene exists. | ## A complete dashboard Everything below is real, running code: ### What the pieces do - **`ContributionToolbar`** forwards `replay` and `reset` to the scene through the template ref. - **`ContributionYearTabs`** is a `v-model` component — bind it to the year your data source uses. - **`ContributionPalettePicker`** is also a `v-model` component; the selected value feeds every other widget through the shared `palette` prop. - **`ContributionStats`** accepts either `:data` (aggregates on the fly) or `:stats` (pre-aggregated by `useContributionStats`). ## Slots Every component accepts slots for the parts you may want to replace. ```vue Fetching contributions… Nothing to show for {{ username }}. ``` ` ` also renders whatever you put in its default slot on top of the canvas, and ` ` exposes `count`, `date` and `rawCount` to its default slot. ## Events ```vue console.log(days.length, 'days rendered')" @hover="(hit) => console.log(hit?.day.date ?? 'left the graph')" @error="(message) => console.warn(message)" /> ``` ## Controls | Input | Action | | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | | Drag | Orbit around the grid. | | Scroll / pinch | Zoom in and out. | | Hover a bar | Highlight it and show the tooltip. | | Right-drag | Pan the camera target. | Keyboard users can tab past the graph to the surrounding controls; the canvas itself is marked `aria-hidden` because the month and weekday labels are exposed as screen-reader text instead.

title: Installation
search: # Installation ## Requirements | Package | Version | Note | | ------------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------- | | `vue` | `^3.4.0` | Peer dependency, must be installed. | | `three` | `>=0.160.0` | Peer dependency, must be installed. | | `tailwindcss` | optional | Only needed if you restyle the tokens. | `vue-contribution-graph-3d` does **not** bundle `vue` or `three`, so your app keeps a single copy of both. ## Package manager ::: code-group ```sh [npm] npm install vue-contribution-graph-3d three ``` ```sh [pnpm] pnpm add vue-contribution-graph-3d three ``` ```sh [yarn] yarn add vue-contribution-graph-3d three ``` ```sh [bun] bun add vue-contribution-graph-3d three ``` ::: ## Import the stylesheet Import the CSS once, next to your application entry file: ```ts // main.ts import { createApp } from 'vue' import App from './App.vue' import 'vue-contribution-graph-3d/style.css' createApp(App).mount('#app') ``` ::: info Why a separate import? The stylesheet is a normal `dist/style.css`. Keeping it out of the JavaScript means your bundler can cache and preload it independently, and it makes it obvious which styles come from this library. ::: ## Register the components ### Globally ```ts import { createApp } from 'vue' import VueContributionGraph3D from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' import 'vue-contribution-graph-3d/style.css' createApp(App).use(VueContributionGraph3D).mount('#app') ``` This registers all eight components, so you can write ` ` anywhere. ### Locally (tree-shakeable) ```vue ``` Only the components you import are pulled into your bundle. The composables and utilities are plain functions and shake out the same way. ## Verifying the install ```vue ``` You should see @torvalds's forest-green grid grow upwards once the profile loads. Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and hover a bar for its exact count. ## Server-side rendering Nothing WebGL runs on the server: - The component renders an empty, correctly sized container during SSR. - The `WebGLRenderer` is only constructed inside `onMounted`, so importing the library never touches `window`, `document` or WebGL while rendering on the server. Importing `three` itself is safe in Node — it is the renderer that needs a canvas. - Stats, legend, toolbar and tabs render real HTML on the server and hydrate normally. No `v-if` or ` ` wrapper is required. ## Version pinning ```jsonc // package.json { "dependencies": { "three": "^0.186.0", "vue-contribution-graph-3d": "^0.1.0", }, } ``` The library is tested against the latest Three.js release, but any version from `0.160.0` onward exposes the APIs it uses (`OrbitControls` from `three/addons`, `SRGBColorSpace`, `ACESFilmicToneMapping`). ## Upgrading ```sh npm install vue-contribution-graph-3d@latest ``` Because every public token and component prop is documented, `npm run typecheck` is usually enough to find what changed.

title: Introduction
search: # Introduction **vue-contribution-graph-3d** turns a year of GitHub activity into a small 3D city. Every day is a bar: quiet days stay flat, busy days tower over their neighbours, and the whole grid grows out of the ground when data arrives. It is a Vue 3 component suite, written in TypeScript, rendered with [Three.js](https://threejs.org/) and styled with [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/). ```md ``` That is the whole idea. Everything else in the package is optional chrome you can compose around it. ## What you get | Component | Purpose | | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | ` ` | The WebGL scene: bars, camera, hover, grow animation. | | ` ` | Status pill plus _Replay animation_ and _Reset view_ buttons. | | ` ` | Less → More intensity swatches. | | ` ` | Total, active days, longest streak and best day. | | ` ` | Switch between the years returned by the API. | | ` ` | Pick between forest, daylight and midnight. | | ` ` | A labelled `@username` input with a submit button. | | ` ` | The hover card, or anything else you put in its slot. | Alongside the components you get four composables — `useGitHubContributions`, `useContributionStats`, `useSampleContributions` and `useReducedMotion` — plus the underlying utilities (`normalizeContributionData`, `computeStats`, …) if you want to drive everything yourself. ## A live example The graph below is rendered by the real component with deterministic sample data, so it works without a network connection. {{ option }} ## Design goals - **Honest 3D.** The height scale is logarithmic so a single contribution is still visible next to your busiest day. Nothing is faked with CSS transforms. - **No surprises in your CSS.** The shipped stylesheet contains only `@theme` tokens and utilities, all namespaced with `cg-`. It never injects a reset and never touches a selector you did not ask for. - **Clean up after itself.** The original demo never released GPU memory. This port disposes geometries, materials, textures, controls, observers and the animation frame on unmount. - **Respect the visitor.** With `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the bars appear at their final height immediately instead of growing. ## Browser support Anything with WebGL1 and `ResizeObserver`. Server-side rendering is supported: the component renders an empty container on the server and creates the Three.js scene only after it mounts.

title: Theming & palettes
search: # Theming & palettes Two independent knobs control how everything looks: - **`palette`** — the color ramp of the bars, the Three.js scene background, and the matching default chrome. - **`theme`** — the light or dark chrome of the surrounding widgets. ```vue ``` ## Palettes | Name | Look | Default chrome | | ---------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------- | | `forest` | Deep greens with a bright mint highlight. | dark | | `daylight` | Soft sage greens on a warm off-white scene. | light | | `midnight` | Violet ramp on a near-black blue scene. | dark | {{ PALETTE_LABELS[option] }} Each swatch of ` ` follows the palette automatically through CSS variables, so you never have to pass colors around by hand. ## Light and dark chrome `theme` accepts `dark`, `light` or `auto` (the default). `auto` follows the palette, which means `daylight` renders light chrome and the other two render dark chrome. Pass an explicit value when you want, for example, a dark toolbar on top of the daylight scene: ```vue ``` Every component exposes the resolved values on its root element: ```html --> ``` Because both attributes are set by the component itself, nesting widgets never causes a theme to leak from a parent. ## The token layer The library ships `dist/style.css`, built from `src/tokens.css`. It contains a `@theme` block of namespaced custom properties plus a small `@layer components` block of overrides — and **nothing else**. No preflight, no base reset, no global element selectors. | Token | Used for | | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | | `--color-cg-page` | Full page background (yours to use). | | `--color-cg-panel` | Panel background (yours to use). | | `--color-cg-field` | Input and tooltip background. | | `--color-cg-selected` | Selected year / palette background. | | `--color-cg-border` | Borders, dividers, the grid frame. | | `--color-cg-text` | Primary text. | | `--color-cg-muted` | Secondary text and legends. | | `--color-cg-accent` | Accent: buttons, stats, focus rings. | | `--color-cg-accent-ink` | Text on top of the accent color. | | `--color-cg-error` | Error text. | | `--color-cg-scene` | WebGL scene background (and its placeholder). | | `--color-cg-level-0 … 4` | The five intensity levels. | | `--font-cg-sans`, `--font-cg-mono` | Component typography (`font-cg-sans`, `font-cg-mono`). | ## Overriding a color Add your own override after the library stylesheet. Attribute selectors win over `:root`, so nothing needs `!important`: ```css /* app.css — imported after 'vue-contribution-graph-3d/style.css' */ [data-cg-theme='dark'] { --color-cg-accent: #7dd3fc; --color-cg-accent-ink: #082f49; } ``` ```ts import 'vue-contribution-graph-3d/style.css' import './app.css' ``` ## Defining your own palette A palette is three things: the ramp used by the WebGL bars, the scene background, and the CSS variables for the legend and the container. ```ts // main.ts — before the first graph mounts import { THEME_PALETTES, THEME_SCENE_COLORS } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' import 'vue-contribution-graph-3d/style.css' import './sunset.css' Object.assign(THEME_PALETTES, { sunset: ['#3b2233', '#7a3350', '#b84f63', '#ef8f6b', '#ffd9a0'], }) Object.assign(THEME_SCENE_COLORS, { sunset: '#1a1119', }) ``` ```css /* sunset.css */ @layer components { [data-cg-palette='sunset'] { --color-cg-scene: #1a1119; --color-cg-level-0: #3b2233; --color-cg-level-1: #7a3350; --color-cg-level-2: #b84f63; --color-cg-level-3: #ef8f6b; --color-cg-level-4: #ffd9a0; } } ``` ```vue ``` An unknown palette name falls back to `forest` everywhere instead of throwing, so a missing entry degrades rather than crashing the scene. ## Reduced motion The grow animation is disabled automatically when the visitor prefers reduced motion — the bars appear at their final height on the first frame. You can still call `replay()` explicitly. ```ts import { useReducedMotion } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const reduced = useReducedMotion() // Ref , live-updating ``` The component wires this up for you; the composable exists for the rare case where you want to fade something else out too. ## Typography Components use `--font-cg-sans` (Arial) and `--font-cg-mono` (Courier New) so they look like the original demo regardless of what your application sets. Override the two variables to match your brand: ```css [data-cg-theme] { --font-cg-sans: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; --font-cg-mono: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; } ```

Exposed Access through a template ref: ```vue ``` | Member | Type | Description | | ----------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | | `ready` | `Ref ` | Whether the scene exists. | | `years` | `Ref ` | Years returned by the API, newest first. | | `year` | `Ref ` | Active year. | | `setYear` | `(year: string \| number) => void` | Switch year. | | `load` | `(username?: string) => Promise ` | Fetch a profile. | | `reload` | `() => void` | Re-fetch the current profile. | | `status` | `Ref ` | `idle`, `loading`, `success`, `error`. | | `error` | `Ref ` | Failure message. | | `replay` | `() => void` | Restart the grow animation. | | `resetView` | `() => void` | Return the camera to its default framing. | ## Loading a profile ```vue console.error(message)" /> ``` ## Rendering without WebGL The `ContributionScene` is constructed in `onMounted`, so the server renders an empty, correctly sized container and the client builds the scene after hydration — no ` ` required. Construction is wrapped in a `try`/`catch`: on machines without WebGL the `error` event fires with a readable message instead of throwing. ## Dispose ` ` releases everything it creates on unmount: geometries, materials, canvas textures, `OrbitControls`, the `ResizeObserver`, pointer listeners and the animation frame. The pill is decorative text rather than a live region, because a status that changes on every animation would be noisy.

title: ContributionTooltip
search: # ContributionTooltip The hover card. ` ` renders one for you by default, but you can disable it with `:show-tooltip="false"` and place your own, or use the component standalone over a 2D chart. move the pointer over this box ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | --------- | -------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- | | `count` | `number` | required | Number of contributions. | | `dateKey` | `string` | `''` | `YYYY-MM-DD`, formatted with `Intl.DateTimeFormat`. | | `x` | `number` | `0` | Horizontal position in CSS pixels. | | `y` | `number` | `0` | Vertical position in CSS pixels. | | `locale` | `string` | `'en'` | BCP 47 locale used for the date. | | `palette` | `string` | `'forest'` | Sets `data-cg-palette`. | | `theme` | `string` | `'auto'` | Light or dark chrome. | The card is positioned with `translate(14px, 14px)` so it never sits under the pointer, and it is `pointer-events-none`, so it can never steal the hover from the bar underneath it. ## Slots The default slot receives the formatted values: ```vue {{ count }} {{ date }} ``` | Slot prop | Value | | ---------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `count` | Ready-to-read label, e.g. `7 contributions`. | | `date` | Formatted date, or `''` without `dateKey`. | | `rawCount` | The raw `count` number. | ## Events None. The tooltip is presentational; the graph emits `hover` with the same `x`/`y` coordinates. ## Accessibility Rendered with `role="status"`, so the count is announced politely when it changes — without the chatter of an `aria-live="assertive"` region that would fire on every pixel of pointer movement.

title: ContributionUserForm
search: # ContributionUserForm A labelled `@username` input with a submit button. It is a controlled component: it never fetches anything itself, it just tells you when the visitor pressed Load profile . last submit: {{ submitted || '—' }} · current model: {{ username || '—' }} ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------- | --------- | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | | `modelValue` | `string` | `''` | The username, with or without the leading `@`. | | `loading` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables the input and shows _Loading…_ | | `label` | `string` | `'GitHub username'` | Label above the input. | | `placeholder` | `string` | `'username'` | Input placeholder. | | `buttonLabel` | `string` | `'Load profile'` | Submit button text. | | `palette` | `string` | `'forest'` | Sets `data-cg-palette`. | | `theme` | `string` | `'auto'` | Sets `data-cg-theme`. | ## Events | Event | Payload | | ------------------- | ------------------ | | `update:modelValue` | `username: string` | | `submit` | `username: string` | The form uses `@submit.prevent`, so pressing Enter in the input emits `submit` and never reloads the page. ## Example ```vue ``` ` ` already watches its prop, so binding the same `v-model` to both the form and the graph is usually all you need. ## Accessibility - The ` ` is associated with the input through a generated, collision-free id (`useId()`), so clicking the label focuses the field. - The `@` is `aria-hidden` decoration; the accessible value is just the username. - `required`, `autocomplete="off"` and `spellcheck="false"` are set for a username field. - The submit button announces its busy state through both `disabled` and its text.

title: ContributionYearTabs
search: # ContributionYearTabs A `v-model` tab list for the years a profile has activity in. Pair it with the `years` and `year` refs exposed by ` `. loading years… selected: {{ year }} · {{ days.length }} cells · loading… ## Props | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ------------ | ------------------------- | ---------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | `modelValue` | `number \| string` | required | The selected year. | | `years` | `Array ` | required | Years to render, in the order you pass them. | | `label` | `string` | `'Contribution years'` | Accessible name of the tab list. | | `palette` | `string` | `'forest'` | Sets `data-cg-palette`. | | `theme` | `string` | `'auto'` | Sets `data-cg-theme`. | ## Events | Event | Payload | | ------------------- | ------------------------ | | `update:modelValue` | `year: number \| string` | Clicking the already selected year emits nothing. ## Example ```vue ``` Or keep the year in your own state and feed it to both, which is what the playground does. ## Accessibility Rendered as `role="tablist"` with one `role="tab"` button per year. The selected tab carries `aria-selected="true"` and every tab is in the natural tab order, so arrow-key semantics can be added on top later without changing the markup.

title: Composables
search: # Composables All four composables are plain functions. They work inside `setup()`, but none of them require a component scope, so you can also use them in tests or in a Pinia store. ## `useGitHubContributions` Reactive state around the community GitHub contributions API (`https://github-contributions-api.jogruber.de/v4/{user}?y=all`). No token required. ```ts import { useGitHubContributions } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const { username, // Ref — normalized handle, `@` stripped year, // Ref — active year years, // Ref — available years, newest first totals, // Ref > — per-year totals days, // Ref — grid for the active year payload, // Ref status, // Ref error, // Ref loading, // Ref load, // (handle?: string) => Promise setYear, // (year: number | string) => void reload, // () => void } = useGitHubContributions({ username: () => username.value, year: () => year.value, }) ``` ### Options | Option | Type | Default | Description | | ---------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | | `username` | `MaybeRefOrGetter ` | `''` | Reactive handle; loads as soon as it is set. | | `year` | `MaybeRefOrGetter ` | current year | Reactive year to display. | | `autoLoad` | `boolean` | `true` | Fetch immediately and when the handle changes. | | `fetchFn` | `typeof fetch` | global | Inject `fetch` for tests, proxies or caching. | ### Behaviour - The requested year is validated against the response; if it does not exist, the newest available year is selected automatically. - Concurrent requests are guarded by a request id and an `AbortController`, so a slow response can never overwrite a newer one. - Failures set `status = 'error'` and a human-readable `error` — `User not found.` for a 404, `Request failed.` otherwise. ## `useContributionStats` ```ts const stats = useContributionStats(() => days.value) // ComputedRef ``` Wraps [`computeStats`](./utilities). Returns zeros for an empty or missing array instead of throwing. ## `useSampleContributions` ```ts const days = useSampleContributions(2025) // ComputedRef const other = useSampleContributions(() => year.value, 42) // custom seed ``` Deterministic sample year — the same arguments always produce the same grid. Every day that has not happened yet stays empty, so the graph is never filled with future activity. ## `useReducedMotion` ```ts const reduced = useReducedMotion() // Ref ``` Tracks `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and updates live. Returns `false` immediately when `window.matchMedia` is unavailable (SSR), and unsubscribes when the current scope is disposed. ::: tip You rarely need this one ` ` calls it internally and hands the value to the scene, which then renders final bar heights instead of growing them. ::: ## `useCgTheme` The internal helper every component uses to resolve and apply its chrome attributes: ```ts const { resolvedTheme, cgAttrs } = useCgTheme(props) ``` ```vue … ``` `cgAttrs` is a computed object containing `data-cg-theme` and `data-cg-palette`. Exported so that custom components can opt into the same token layer.

title: Utilities & constants
search: # Utilities & constants Everything below is a pure function or a frozen value. No Three.js, no Vue, no globals — safe to use in tests, in a worker, or to drive a 2D fallback that matches the 3D scene exactly. ## Data helpers ### `normalizeContributionData(entries, year)` Expands sparse `{ date, count }` pairs into a complete rectangular week grid. ```ts import { normalizeContributionData } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' const days = normalizeContributionData([{ date: '2025-09-21', count: 4 }], 2025) ``` - Columns run Sunday-first from the Sunday on or before January 1. - Padding days from the neighbouring years are included with `count: 0` and `isOutsideYear: true`. - Days that have not happened yet are flagged `isFuture: true` and never carry a count. - Missing and malformed entries are ignored rather than throwing. ### `getWeeksForYear(year)` Number of week columns a year needs (53 or 54). ### `startOfDay(date)` · `startOfWeek(date)` · `toLocalDateKey(date)` Local-time helpers used by the normalizer. `toLocalDateKey` produces `YYYY-MM-DD` **in local time**, which is what GitHub's payload uses. ## Level and height helpers ### `getContributionLevel(count)` Returns `0`–`4` using the GitHub buckets: `0`, `1–3`, `4–7`, `8–13`, `14+`. ### `getBarHeight(count, maxCount)` ```ts count === 0 ? 0.1 : 0.24 + (Math.log1p(count) / Math.log1p(maxCount)) * (10.5 - 0.24) ``` The busiest day always lands exactly on `MAX_VISIBLE_HEIGHT` and an empty day on `ZERO_HEIGHT`. `maxCount — 5 levels each THEME_SCENE_COLORS, // Record PALETTE_THEME, // Record PALETTE_LABELS, // Record PALETTE_NAMES, // ['forest', 'daylight', 'midnight'] resolveTheme, // (palette, theme?) => 'dark' | 'light' getPaletteColors, // safe lookup, falls back to forest getSceneColor, // safe lookup, falls back to forest } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' ``` ## Constants | Constant | Value | Meaning | | ----------------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------- | | `WEEKS_PER_YEAR` | `53` | Maximum week columns. | | `DAYS_PER_WEEK` | `7` | Rows per column. | | `CELL_SIZE` | `0.9` | Bar edge length in world units. | | `CELL_GAP` | `0.3` | Space between bars. | | `CELL_STEP` | `1.2` | `CELL_SIZE + CELL_GAP`. | | `ZERO_HEIGHT` | `0.1` | Height of an empty day. | | `MIN_BAR_HEIGHT` | `0.24` | Height of the first contribution. | | `MAX_VISIBLE_HEIGHT` | `10.5` | Height of the busiest day. | | `DEFAULT_GROW_DURATION` | `2400` | Animation length in ms. | | `LOOP_DELAY` | `700` | Pause between loops in ms. | | `LEVEL_COUNT` | `5` | Number of intensity levels. | | `LEVEL_THRESHOLDS` | `[3, 7, 13]` | Upper bounds of levels 1–3. | ## Three.js classes Advanced use only — these are exported for people who want to host the scene themselves. ```ts import { ContributionScene, GrowthAnimator, easeOutCubic } from 'vue-contribution-graph-3d' ``` ### `new ContributionScene(container, options?)` | Method | Purpose | | ------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | `setData(days)` | Replace the rendered year. | | `setPalette(name)` / `setTheme(theme)` | Retint bars, scene, lights and labels. | | `setAnimation({ animate, loop, duration })` | Update the grow animation. | | `setAxisLabels(visible)` | Toggle the month/weekday sprites. | | `setGridFrame(visible)` | Toggle the outline. | | `setPaused(paused)` | Freeze interaction and looping while loading. | | `setHoverListener(fn)` | Receive `{ day, level, x, y }` or `null`. | | `replay()` · `resetView()` | Animation and camera. | | `dispose()` | Release every GPU resource and listener. | ### `GrowthAnimator` The time-based grow animation, deliberately free of Three.js so it can be unit tested: ```ts const animator = new GrowthAnimator({ duration: 2400, loop: true }) animator.replay(blocks) // blocks: { targetHeight, scale, position }[] animator.tick(performance.now(), blocks) ``` `easeOutCubic(progress)` is the easing it uses, exported so a matching 2D chart can share it.
